title: Core supersession decision kernel
description: Objective: land the pure core decision surface for graph supersession: the closed disposition vocabulary, monotonic epoch/predecessor-successor binding, explicit safe-carry evidence, deterministic authority hash, and frozen atomic decision/refusal result. Deliverable: create packages/core/src/supersession/supersession-engine.ts, its CommonJS-compatible .js bridge, a focused production-surface test, and a curated named export block in packages/core/src/index.ts. The kernel must compose `evaluateCarryForward` from policy/approval-invalidation.ts, map every changed or UNKNOWN authority/input fact to the existing `SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED` code, and use `REVISION_REBOUND` for stale/non-monotonic or predecessor/successor rebound. Consumer task: task-1df0622e87cf42beae2cd82280e9ff99 composes this kernel into `graph.supersede`. NOT in scope: graph reducer/state migration, scheduler attempt/effect/resource/budget application, daemon persistence, UI, or new runtime error vocabulary. Owned paths: packages/core/src/supersession/supersession-engine.ts, supersession-engine.js, supersession-engine.test.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: The core exports a frozen closed disposition-kind tuple containing exactly ADD, CARRY, REQUALIFY, REEXECUTE, CHANGE, and REMOVE, plus immutable predecessor/successor epoch, safe-carry, decision, and refusal types from one curated core-root block.

The production kernel accepts only a distinct successor at exactly predecessor epoch + 1 with an exact predecessor revision/content binding; stale, skipped, overflowed, malformed, duplicate, or rebound inputs return frozen `REVISION_REBOUND` at the kernel layer without an activation decision.

Every CARRY entry must have explicit matching authority and input-binding evidence accepted by production `evaluateCarryForward`; changed, missing, or UNKNOWN evidence returns frozen `SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED` at the kernel layer, while non-CARRY entries cannot smuggle carry authority.

An accepted decision is deeply frozen, deterministically ordered/hash-bound to the predecessor, successor, epoch, dispositions, and safe carry bindings, and exposes no overlapping predecessor authority or mutable aliases.

Focused tests cover happy path, each refusal guard, permutation determinism, duplicate/empty/overflow boundaries, and an exhaustive six-kind production-surface sweep with positive case count; mutation drills for epoch and stored-evidence/carry guards go red; fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0 and every production file is <=250 lines.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights: `evaluateCarryForward(value, supportedCanonicalizerVersions)` accepts an exact seven-field `CarryForwardInput`; malformed input returns INPUT_INVALID, while semantic failures return `{ok:true, value:{valid:false, reasonCodes}}`. Do not require successor content to differ: a distinct revision can legitimately retain identical graph bytes. Guard accessors/proxies/cycles/sparse arrays, safe-integer overflow, Unicode/code-unit ordering, duplicate supported versions, and mutable aliases. Hash every semantic field with explicit null/boolean framing and pin a golden vector so a future omission cannot remain green.
